scope: Meaning-bearing temporal/subject comparison of the joy clause in 35:14, in the retained Hebrew unit 35:10-15. Not historical priority of the Hebrew/Greek literary editions or certification of the entire verse.
source_text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣/י יְהוִ֑ה כִּ/שְׂמֹ֨חַ֙ כָּל הָ/אָ֔רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֖ה אֶעֱשֶׂה לָּֽ/ךְ־־׃
close_gloss: Thus said the Lord YHWH: as/when the rejoicing of all the earth/land, a desolation I will make you. This diagnostic gloss does not settle who rejoices or the temporal relation.

context_english_summary: The addressee is Mount Seir/Edom. In 35:10-13 it claims the two nations/lands and reviles the mountains of Israel; God announces judgment. Verse 15 compares Edom's rejoicing over Israel's desolation with what God will do to Edom. This summary is context, not approved replacement English.

candidates.M: Just as you rejoiced over the whole land, I will make you desolate.
candidates.T: When the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.
candidates.P: As the whole earth rejoiced, I will make you desolate.

policy.priority: Meaning, grammatical agency and unsupported additions first; preserved ambiguity, literary function, naturalness and consistency next. Readability serves fidelity.
policy.source: Retain WLC consonants, pointing and segmentation; evaluate different syntactic interpretations explicitly. Do not insert a noun tav or replace initial kaf with bet.
policy.boundaries: Only the joy/judgment clause is compared. The divine-title formula and verse 15 reader wording are not certified by this comparison. Source priority, chapter order and canon remain separate.
policy.notes: Recommend disclosure of a consequential alternative rather than claiming the selected English exhausts the Hebrew. Do not add the occasion/cause of joy to the main clause without source support.

evidence_limits: The local XML annotates כ/שמח as Qal infinitive construct, not a finite past form. GKC 114e/q allows temporal kaf with infinitive and contextual time; this does not require one temporal reading here.

GKC 115e describes a following noun as a normal subject of an infinitive; 115a/b and footnote 2 also allow object constructions and contextually supplied subjects. A following noun is not mechanically always the subject.
The longer Hebrew verse 15 explicitly makes Edom the rejoicer over Israel's desolation. Assess whether 14 anticipates that comparison or sets up a contrast, without assuming either relationship.

A published literary-edition interpretation takes whole land in 14 as the object of joy. Candidate M is our idiomatic test of that interpretation, not a direct quotation; its supplied subject and relation require evaluation.

P967's Greek has a joy phrase and lacks the longer 15a comparison. Compatibility with one English choice does not prove its Hebrew source or priority. Masada preserves substantial longer 15a wording, but its distinguishing noun tav in 14 is supplied in the consulted edition.
No new manuscript transcription, fresh HALOT consultation or generated-image evidence is supplied. These are grammar and interpretation controls, not statistical confidence in original wording.
